name: cmux.terminal.backend/1
docs: Bytes mode (ghostty-next-switch.md section 3, cloud-app.md): the backend carries raw terminal bytes; the local session host parses them, answers terminal queries unless capabilities.answers_queries, and owns snapshots and the journal. An app backend runs as the app's server (implements with server: true) and needs the restricted scope terminal:backend. No method or host op gives the backend a secret or a signature: for connection handles of kind ssh the host owns the SSH transport (it dials, checks the pinned host key and authenticates with the user's key) and the backend gets a channel (hostOps). Rust traits TerminalBackend, ByteTerminal and HostChannels in the crate cmux-terminal-iface (synchronous, frames pulled with take_frames); the daemon side is cmux-tui-core terminal_backend.

props.target: string (an opaque connection handle conn_..., or a backend-defined id such as a cloud machine id; never a host name typed by a user or an agent)

methods.open: removed from the wire (2026-10-04, P1): the app opens a terminal with the host op cmux.terminal.backend.open; the Rust trait TerminalBackend::open stays as the app's own shape
methods.resume: removed from the wire: host op cmux.terminal.backend.resume
methods.write: removed: input is data frames on the terminal channel (dataPlane), within the backend's in credit
methods.resize: host.event cmux.terminal.backend.resize {terminal, cols, rows, cell_width_px?, cell_height_px?}: the session host's grid changed (capabilities.resize)
methods.signal: not sent yet: the session host sends no signals; Ctrl-C and similar keys are input bytes
methods.close: host.event cmux.terminal.backend.close {terminal}: the session host closed the terminal (a kill, or no client placed it within 60 s); the terminal has already ended on the host

kinds.description: Target kinds this implementation serves; the registry ids are app:<app>/<kind>. Default deny: a kind not listed is never routed here.

openOps.description: The app's own catalog ops whose user runs may open a link or terminal. The host accepts an open_token only when it was minted for a user-origin run of one of these ops (default deny); a token from any other op, such as a list read, is denied.

status: draft: shapes chosen by the ghostty-next lead (2026-10-04, revised with the SSH sample's gaps: offsets, typed host key refusal, exit signal, answers_queries, host-owned SSH transport with no signing op; 2026-10-04 later: credit-based data frames, host-picked terminal ids, denied for undeclared kinds); refined with the cmux Cloud and third-party sample backends before the interface is public; 2026-10-04 later: terminal open/resume are app -> host ops, host channels open per terminal, resize/close are host events

eventShapes.output: data frames on the terminal channel (dataPlane), within the session host's out credit; offset is the running total since open and continues across resume
eventShapes.exit: end {terminal, exit: {code?, signal?, core_dumped, message?}}: code when the far end sent an exit status; signal is the name without SIG; message is far-end text, at most 4 KiB, shown and never parsed

capabilities.answers_queries: bool: true only when the far end answers DA, DSR and OSC color queries itself; then the session host parses but never replies. A shell over a PTY or SSH is false.

errors.hostKey: {decision: unknown|changed, fingerprint: "SHA256:..."}: typed host key refusal; the host shows its accept sheet from these fields. Nothing reached the far shell.
errors.denied: {reason}: a kind not in options.kinds, a revoked handle, or a failed host check

hostOps.cmux.terminal.backend.open: ({kind, target, open_token}) -> {terminal, window_bytes}. Direction: app server -> host. The host consumes open_token first (issued to this app, single use, 60 s; any attempt burns it), then checks that it was minted for an op in options.openOps, that the app implements this interface with its server and holds the terminal:backend grant, that kind is in options.kinds, and target (1 to 256 bytes, no control characters); at most 64 terminals per app. The session host assigns the terminal id, creates the terminal with no tab (it parses, answers queries, keeps the journal and snapshots) at its own grid, and broadcasts apps-terminal {terminal, id, app, target, run_key} to its clients; the client whose user run has run_key places it in its own focused workspace; a terminal no client placed within 60 s is closed. Output is data frames for channel=terminal; the app's end frame (exit or lost) ends the terminal after its last output.
hostOps.cmux.terminal.backend.resume: ({terminal, resume_token, open_token}) -> {window_bytes, offset}: after a user run of an op in options.openOps ("disconnected, click to reconnect"); nothing resumes on its own. v1: the token is consumed and checked, then the host answers unsupported (reviving an ended session-host terminal is not built).
hostOps.cmux.terminal.channel.open: ({terminal, connection, pty: {term, cols, rows}, command?}) -> {channel, window_bytes} (P2): only for an open terminal this app holds (its open consumed the token). The host resolves the connection handle, dials, checks the pinned host key (else hostKey), authenticates with the user's credential and opens a PTY channel. The backend never sees the host name, the key or a signature. v1: the transport is not built and answers unavailable {retryable: false}.
hostOps.open_token: issued by the host for one open or resume of one terminal after the user's gesture (a user-origin run of an op in options.openOps); host ops refuse a missing, expired, reused or other app's token, or one minted for an op outside options.openOps

dataPlane.frames: Data moves as frames on the app host's stream (binary payload), never as op calls. Per channel, in order: data {channel, offset, bytes} (offset = running byte total after this frame, per direction), credit {channel, direction: in|out, bytes} and end {channel, exit? | lost?} (exactly once, after the last data). channel is a host channel (hostOps), a terminal (backend output and input) or a connector link.
dataPlane.credit: The receiver grants bytes; the sender keeps at most the granted, not yet acknowledged bytes in flight and never sends past them. Each direction starts with window_bytes (from the open answer, 64 KiB to 1 MiB, default 256 KiB); the receiver sends credit as it consumes data. Data past the credit is a protocol violation: the receiver ends the channel with lost {reason: "credit", retryable: false}. No frame or op waits.
dataPlane.backpressure: End to end: the session host grants output credit for a terminal only while its viewers and journal keep up; a backend grants host-channel out credit only from its own terminal credit, so a slow viewer stops the far end (SSH window) instead of growing a buffer. Input runs the other way the same way.
dataPlane.continuity: A receiver checks offsets: a gap or an overlap ends the channel with lost. resume continues the offsets of the resumed terminal.
